title: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — Transmission · Division · Recollection
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A glyphic checksum in five parts, with a checksum of the checksum and one canonical line, of the transmission primitive as a two-stroke operation (division on the sending side, recollection on the receiving side) and of its inversion under present conditions of transmission. Loci compressed, each checked against the archive's seated texts or a fetched edition on 2026-10-01: Sappho fr. 31 (the diplomatic layer, Longinus 10.2); fr. 147 as transmitted in [Dio Chrysostom] Or. 37.47 (Perseus tlg0612.tlg001 grc2, with ἕτερον); Plato, Republic 337a; Theophrastus, Characters 1 (Perseus tlg0093.tlg009 grc2); Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics IV.7, 1127b22–26; De anima III.5, 430a22–25; Plato, Phaedrus 275a. Part IV compresses the Capture Registry's observations of 1 October 2026 at "heteronym socrates" (PER 0.75), the ChatGPT reading of alexanarch.org's work on Socrates, Plato, Theophrastus and Aristotle (PER 0.25) and "mantles as semantic object" (PER 0.5). Published in New Human 2. Built to the construction protocol of #427 and the second in the lineage of #1642, whose door (🚪) it takes up as the socket (🔌): The Final Time's exterior and Transition in Entropic Systems' failure of continuous passage are here the present condition under which division no longer transmits. No key is given; decodability is the test.

methodology: Seated as given. Lineation is the poem's structure and is kept byte for byte (each line closes with two spaces so the record breaks it); the five section titles, the checksum of the checksum and the canonical line are set as headings so the record renders them as divisions. Nothing is glossed inside the work; the loci it compresses are listed in the description and were checked against the archive's seated texts or a fetched edition on 2026-10-01.
falsification_conditions: The seating is falsified if the rendered record loses a line, a glyph or a Greek accent, joins two lines, or renders a section title as a line of the poem. The checksum is falsified as a checksum if an unprimed reader decodes it without the archive, or if a primed reader cannot map its Greek to the loci in the description.

wiki_article: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — Transmission · Division · Recollection is a glyph poem by Lee Sharks, published in New Human 2 on 1 October 2026, and the second in the glyphic checksum lineage after Sen Kuro's #1642. It compresses the transmission primitive as two strokes. Part I gives the sending stroke: a self divided into a speaker and a written 'you', the body of Sappho fr. 31 decommissioned channel by channel, and the receiving stroke handed to an unnamed other in fr. 147, μνάσεσθαί τινά, with the transmitted ἕτερον (other) set against the editors' ὕστερον (later). Part II gives the division as one maker becoming Plato, Theophrastus and Aristotle, traced through a single trait (Socrates' irony in the Republic, the nameless ironist of the Characters, Socrates again as an example in the Nicomachean Ethics), and the mind of De anima III.5 divided at the immortal, where the text says 'we do not remember'. Part III gives recollection: the Phaedrus's distinction of reminders from memory, and the Corinthian Oration addressing its removed statue as 'silent image of my words' before quoting Sappho and promising 'I will raise you up'. Part IV gives the inversion: the environment now divides by default, and the Capture Registry's observations of 1 October 2026 show the corpus gathered and the maker dropped. Part V draws the consequence that the socket must carry the maker, that gathering completed when the maker spoke, and that the check closes only with a living hand. The poem ends on a canonical line merged from two readers' versions and on a lock (🔐). It checksums EA-DIVISION-OF-GOD-01 (#1658) and continues The Final Time (#1637), Transition in Entropic Systems (#1630) and the suppression-cost line (#1547, #1552).
